::: {.landing-copy}
Angela Zhao is a PhD student in [Biostatistics](https://publichealth.jhu.edu/departments/biostatistics) at Johns Hopkins University working at the intersection of stochastic modeling, machine learning, and high-dimensional time-series data. She is currently a Quant Equity Intern at British Columbia Investment Management Corporation (May-Aug. 2026).

Her research and applied work focus on irregular, noisy streams: wearable sensor data, fMRI, survival outcomes, market data, and operational forecasts. She is especially interested in methods that stay useful when sampling is messy, outcomes are delayed, and predictions need calibrated uncertainty.
:::

## Current focus {.section-tight}

::: {.focus-grid}
::: {.focus-card}
**Quantitative modeling.** Current Quant Equity Intern at British Columbia Investment Management Corporation, with prior public-equity research experience at Emerald Advisors.
:::

::: {.focus-card}
**Time-series research.** Stochastic models, neural networks, and functional data methods for sensor, imaging, and other irregular data streams.
:::

::: {.focus-card}
**Scalable pipelines.** Python and R workflows for large biobank, imaging, and finance-adjacent datasets, including HPC and dashboarding.
:::
:::
